name: AltoScribe – AI Product Descriptions for WooCommerce
author: The Really Useful App Company

sections.description:
No API key. No account. No setup. Unlike almost every other AI product-description plugin, which makes you sign up for OpenAI or Anthropic and paste in your own paid API key, AltoScribe runs the AI on our hosted service, so there is nothing to configure. You generate each description with one click from the product screen, with 10 free every month. Paid plans add higher monthly allowances for larger catalogues, plus one-off credit top-ups for big imports.

Each result is a short description plus a long description, written from the product’s own name, attributes and categories. You review and edit before anything is saved, and an existing description is never overwritten unless you tick “Replace existing descriptions when applying”, so it is safe to run across a live store.

Watch it work: a short demo on a test store, with an AI-generated voiceover.

Do one product from the product editor, or generate for many products at once from the bulk screen: filter by category, stock status, or “missing description only”, generate to a staging area, then accept, skip or edit each result. A big run can be paused and resumed.

  • No API key or third-party account. The AI runs on our service.
  • One click to generate a short and long description from the product editor.
  • Bulk generation with a filtered, resumable queue and a review grid.
  • Review, edit and accept before anything is written to the product.
  • Never overwrites existing copy unless you ask, and one-click undo of the last apply.
  • Tone and length presets, plus optional keywords to weave in.
  • Privacy-friendly: to generate a description we send the product’s name, attributes and categories, with a site ID (a hash of your site URL) and the plugin version. The External services section below lists everything that is sent.
  • 10 free descriptions every month; paid plans add higher monthly allowances, plus credit top-ups for big imports.

AI-generated content can be inaccurate. AltoScribe writes from the product’s own name, attributes and categories, and shows you every description to review before it is saved. Always check descriptions for accuracy before publishing.

External services

This plugin connects to the Really Useful App Company API to generate product descriptions. It is required for the plugin’s core feature.

  • What is sent and when: the plugin sends the product name, its attributes and categories to the API on each of these actions, and nothing else triggers a send of your content:
    • when you click “Generate description” on a product
    • when you run a bulk generation from the Products screen
  • Also sent: a site ID (a hash of your site URL) for usage counting, and the plugin version, so we can tell which release a report relates to. We treat the site ID as personal data, because it can be matched to your site’s address. Our privacy policy explains how we use it. Whether this site’s review prompt was shown, snoozed, dismissed or clicked is also sent, so we can tell whether that prompt is working. It records the site, not the individual user, and says nothing about what you did on WordPress.org afterwards. If you choose to give us an email address, it is sent on its own, only when you submit your email address on the settings screen. It is optional, you are asked once (and again only after we have deleted it), and every feature keeps working if you skip or dismiss it. It is sent only if you tick the sign-up box, together with the wording you agreed to. We use it to send release notes and product updates and to give you a way to reach us. These emails are sent from our Microsoft 365 mailbox. You can unsubscribe from any message, and we delete it 24 months after your last contact with us. Whether this site’s email prompt was shown, dismissed or submitted is also sent, so we can tell whether it is working; it does not include the address itself.
  • Where it goes: the API (default https://api.thereallyusefulappcompany.com), which uses Anthropic as an AI subprocessor to generate the text.
  • Terms / privacy: https://www.thereallyusefulappcompany.com/altoscribe/terms , https://www.thereallyusefulappcompany.com/altoscribe/privacy , https://www.anthropic.com/legal/privacy

Nothing is sent until you click generate or run a bulk generation. If you choose to give us an email address, it is sent when you submit it.
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate AltoScribe. WooCommerce must be installed and active.
  2. Go to Settings → AltoScribe, review the external-service notice, and set your default tone, length and keywords.
  3. Edit a product and click Generate description in the AltoScribe box, review it, then click Apply to product.
  4. For many products at once, go to Products → AltoScribe Bulk.
  5. (Optional) Enter a paid-plan licence key to raise your monthly allowance.
sections.faq:
Do I need an AI API key?

No. The AI runs on our service. There is nothing to sign up for and no key to paste in.

Is it free?

You get 10 free descriptions every month. Paid plans add higher monthly allowances for larger catalogues, plus one-off credit top-ups for big one-time imports.

Will it overwrite my existing descriptions?

No. AltoScribe never overwrites a description that already has content unless you tick “Replace existing descriptions when applying”. You can also undo the last apply.

Does it change my products automatically?

No. Every description is shown to you to review and edit, and nothing is written to a product until you accept it.

Does it work with my product attributes?

Yes. Descriptions are written from the product’s name, its WooCommerce attributes and its categories.

What does it send?

The product’s name, attributes and categories, with a site ID (a hash of your site URL) for usage counting and the plugin version. The External Services section lists everything that is sent.
sections.changelog:
1.0.23

  • Fixed: deleting the plugin now also removes the notice dismissals, review-prompt settings, unapplied results and any bulk run in progress that it stored, so nothing is left behind.
  • Changed: shared code updated to match the other Alto plugins. Nothing changes in how descriptions are generated or applied.

1.0.22

  • Changed: the settings screen now says the site ID is treated as personal data, as our privacy policy does.
  • Changed: small wording fixes on the settings screen, the bulk screen and in the list of our other plugins.
  • Fixed: on a site with more than one Alto plugin, an older Alto plugin could supply this plugin’s shared code, which could silently switch off newer features such as the monthly-limit notice. Each Alto plugin now uses its own copy.
  • Added: an optional sign-up for release notes and product updates by email, offered once on the settings screen after you have used the plugin a few times. You sign up by ticking a box, every feature works without it, and you can unsubscribe from any message.

1.0.15

  • Changed: an update to the code shared across the Alto plugins. No change to how AltoScribe works.

1.0.14

  • Fixed: with a licence key saved, the usage panel could read “Not confirmed yet” indefinitely and hide the upgrade and credits button. It now shows your plan after your next generation.
  • Added: a notice when this site has used its free descriptions for the month, on the Dashboard, the settings screen and the product screens, with the date it resets.
  • Added: once 80% of the month’s allowance is used, the product screens show how many descriptions are left.
  • Changed: the request for a review is not shown while the site is at its monthly limit.

1.0.13

  • Fixed: a licence key that our service does not recognise is no longer shown as “Pro”. The plugin now says the key was not recognised and keeps the upgrade link visible, instead of silently putting you on the free allowance with no way to correct it.
  • Changed: your licence key is no longer shown in full or left in an editable box. Settings now shows only the last four characters, and replacing the key takes a deliberate click on “Update key”, so it cannot be typed over by accident. Removing a key is its own checkbox.
  • Added: the licence field now says to paste your subscription key when you also hold credit packs. Credits are held against your account, so they are found either way, but a credit-pack key on its own puts the site on the free monthly allowance.

1.0.11

  • Fixed: the address the plugin uses to reach our AI service is now required to be https, both when it is saved and every time it is read. Only an administrator could ever have changed it, and the default has always been secure, but an insecure address entered by hand would have sent your licence key and your content unencrypted. An address that is not https is now refused and the secure default is used instead.
  • Fixed: a bulk run checked once that you can edit products, then generated for every product in the run. It now checks your permission on each product individually, and counts anything you cannot edit as skipped. This only makes a difference on a store where several people manage different products.
  • Fixed: on the bulk screen, Start generation, Preview count and Resume are now greyed out while a run is in progress. They previously stayed active and a click did nothing.
  • Fixed: the panel no longer labels your product’s existing description as “AI-generated”. That note now appears only for text AltoScribe has just written.
  • Fixed: the product panel now loads the script it depends on rather than relying on another plugin or screen to load it.

1.0.6

  • Added: a Settings link on the Plugins screen, and a short notice after activation saying where to go.

1.0.5

  • Added: the plugin now reports whether this site’s review prompt was shown, snoozed, dismissed or clicked, so we can tell whether the prompt is working at all. It rides the request the plugin already makes, so no new outbound request is made and no new action triggers a send. It records the site rather than the individual user, and nothing about what happens on WordPress.org afterwards.

1.0.4

  • Fixed: when the AI could not be reached, the description was still labelled “AI-generated”. It now says plainly that the text was assembled from the product’s own fields and is worth rewriting.
  • Added: the plugin now reports its own version with each request, so we can tell which release a problem relates to. No personal data is involved.
  • Housekeeping: the usage panel now comes from the shared Alto component instead of a private copy, and the list of actions that send data is checked automatically against the code before every release.

1.0.3

  • Compatibility: tested with WordPress 7.1.

1.0.2

  • Corrected the AltoGraph name in the list of our other plugins shown on the settings screen.
  • Small wording tidy-ups on the settings screen and the product editor.

1.0.1

  • Added a usage panel on the settings screen showing your monthly allowance, any credits, and a quick link to upgrade.
  • Added an optional, dismissible prompt inviting an honest review after you’ve generated a few times. No tracking; dismiss any time.

1.0.0

  • Initial release: single-product and bulk AI product descriptions, review-before-save with never-overwrite and undo, tone/length presets and keywords, hosted AI with no API key.
